info.name: BLUE V1 - Payment
info.description:
BLUE V1 Phase 6A Payment Core endpoints, generated from the actual implementation in backend/routes/api.php, backend/app/Http/Controllers/Api/V1/Payment, backend/app/Actions/Payment, and verified against backend/tests/Feature/Payment. See docs/api-contracts/payments-v1.md for the full written contract.

Stripe is the approved BLUE V1 payment provider, but no Stripe account/keys are configured yet - none are needed to exercise this collection, since local/testing environments bind a deterministic fake gateway. Create Payment requires the caller's ACTIVE cart to already be ready_for_payment (run the Checkout collection first: Add Cart Item, Save Checkout Location, Create Appointment Hold). The request body carries NO amount/currency/status field - the server derives everything from the cart. The Idempotency-Key header defaults to a fresh {{$guid}} per send; replace it with a fixed value across two sends to observe idempotent reuse (same payment returned, HTTP 200 instead of 201).

When the response includes a fresh provider initiation (a new attempt, or a same-key retry that reached the provider), data.payment also carries client_secret and publishable_key - the two values a future Flutter Stripe PaymentSheet integration needs for that one payment. Neither is ever present on GET /payments/{payment}. Against the fake gateway (no real Stripe account yet) these are deterministic fake values, not real Stripe tokens - this collection cannot be used to complete an actual PaymentSheet confirmation.

This collection does not include a webhook request: POST /v1/payments/webhooks/stripe is provider-authenticated (Stripe-Signature over the raw body), not something a manually-sent Postman request can produce a valid signature for without the real STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, which is deliberately not configured yet. Manually posting to this route without a valid signature only proves the route rejects unsigned requests - it is NOT evidence of real Stripe webhook integration. Webhook behavior is covered by backend/tests/Feature/Payment/WebhookTest.php (fake gateway's own signing scheme) and backend/tests/Feature/Payment/StripeAdapterTest.php (real Stripe\Webhook signing, transport-mocked, no live account) instead.

request.description: Revalidates the caller's ACTIVE cart is ready_for_payment (server-side, ignoring any previous GET /checkout response), freezes an immutable checkout snapshot, renews the appointment hold, transitions the cart ACTIVE -> CHECKOUT, and starts a payment with the configured provider. No amount/currency/payment_status/provider_status/success/checkout_reference/cart_uuid field is ever read from the request body - sending one is rejected with 422 so client bugs are obvious rather than silently ignored. Requires the Idempotency-Key header (a UUID); resending the exact same key returns the same payment attempt (200) instead of creating a second one or calling the provider again. 404 when there is no ACTIVE cart and no open payment attempt for this customer; 409 when this customer already has an open payment attempt for a CHECKOUT cart and a different Idempotency-Key was used; 422 when not ready_for_payment or when the Idempotency-Key is malformed/reused for another customer.

Reads the current safe state of one payment attempt - uuid, checkout_reference, status (PENDING/SUCCESSFUL/FAILED/CANCELLED/REFUNDED), requested_amount, currency, expires_at, provider. Never returns the checkout snapshot, its hash, the idempotency key, or any provider secret. Ownership-scoped through the payment's cart's customer_user_id - a foreign or unknown payment_uuid returns 404, identically, whether it belongs to another customer or does not exist at all.
